entities.summary:
Bernardim Ribeiro was a Renaissance Portuguese poet and writer who flourished in the court of King Manuel I of Portugal (1495-1521) and was known for his lyric poetry and satirical works.

Born into a noble family, Ribeiro received a humanist education and became a prominent figure in the Portuguese literary scene of the 16th century. His poetry often explored themes of love, morality, and social commentary, and he was praised by his contemporaries for his wit and sophistication.

Ribeiro's work had a lasting impact on Portuguese literature, influencing generations of writers and poets. His legacy can be seen in the works of later poets, such as Luís de Camões, who built upon Ribeiro's style and themes.

In the annals of Portuguese history, Ribeiro's contributions serve as a testament to the country's rich cultural heritage and its enduring legacy in the world of literature.
